Five wrong passwords: Frappe locks the user for 15 min, on every kiosk.
A valid Frappe user who is not on this Kiosk Profile is refused.
After 9.5 min without a tap the kiosk warns, then logs out at 10 min.
Cloud setup with the internet down: values freeze, saves queue on the tablet.
A save that fails keeps the entry and retries; the button shows the attempt.
Closing the kiosk session: a supervisor reviews the shift totals and open items.
A cleared alarm nobody acknowledged stays listed and keeps escalating.
Shelved alarms with who shelved them, why, and until when.
Closed alarms with how long they took to acknowledge.
An unacknowledged alarm past its response time goes up a level.
A flood: downstream alarms are held under the trip so the four that matter stay visible.
The calm state: no active alarms, with the last one named.
A newly paired plant before its first message: nothing is shown as a value.
Between live and offline: data 30 s to 5 min old, shown as delayed.
A plant with tags but no layout: live values elsewhere work, the layout area invites one.
Both samples passed; only the Quality Inspector can release the line.
QA released; the PLC interlock is reset only by the key at the panel.
Restarted after the key reset; the trip closes with its quality hold.
A failed release sample sends recovery back to sampling.
Every lot decided: the hold can be closed and its stock moves posted.
A closed hold shows what was posted and closes its trip.
A release with deviation waits for a second person, the Factory Manager.
If ERPNext refuses a stock move, the hold stays open and says why.
After picking a reason: the row updates and a short confirmation shows.
Every stop today has a reason: the badge says so instead of disappearing.
Start a run from a work order; it stays disabled while a hold blocks it.
Ending a run shows what will post to ERPNext before it does.
Ended but not posted: counts are kept and the ERPNext error is shown.
The same run with ERPNext off: no work order, nothing posted.
Submitted and waiting for the incoming supervisor to accept.
Accepted: the shift closes and the handover becomes read-only.
Without a submitted handover the shift cannot close.
A new layout: start from the Process Flow or by dragging symbols.
Generated from the Process Flow; a notice says what was placed and what to check.
Preview shows the draft as operators will see it, with live values, before publishing.
Publishing shows what changed and any problems left.
Published: the version is live and the previous one is kept.
Two people editing: the second publisher merges or saves a new version.
Roles below Factory Manager propose a change through the workflow.
A rejected proposal keeps the reason and leaves the live version unchanged.
With no workflow for their role, lower roles can only read the flow.
Validation blocks approval while any path ends without a filler, drain or return.
Step 1: the plant's name, code, place and warehouse.
Step 3: pair the plant's edge box with a code.
Step 4: the first layout, from the template, another plant or blank.
Finished: what was created and what happens next.
The grid is back: the switch is read from ATS-1 and the generator stops.
Without an ATS, controller or meter signal, the source is shown as not measured.
Diesel under its reorder point, with the request already raised.
Test now fails: the message says which side did not answer.
The uplink is down: the buffer fills on the box and screens say how old the data is.
An unused pairing code expires after 24 h; a new one is one click.
A changed field shows a save bar; closing asks before discarding.
Uplink down on the box itself: the buffer grows, local work carries on.
With the clock unsynced the box keeps reading but holds uploads.
First boot: the only job is to enter the pairing code.
An update in progress, with the automatic rollback stated.
One device stops answering: which port, since when, and what still works.
A scan that finds nothing says what it tried and what to check.
Local logins lock after five wrong passwords, with the way to reset on the box.
A device that stops answering marks its tags Bad and points to the edge page.
A value outside the sensor range is marked Bad and pauses its alarms.
Devices the edge box found arrive as suggestions to review.
The history of config versions sent to the box, with restore.
Loading: rows keep their shape so nothing jumps when data arrives.
Empty: says the plants are reporting, so empty means calm, not broken.
No results for a search or filter, with a way out.
A failed load says what failed and that alarms are still being raised.
